To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tri-imidazole AR-1-1-144 can recognize a T:G mismatch in a DNA duplex and that the Im-Im pair is a recognition motif for the T:G mismatch.

(1) an Im/Im side-by-side pair can recognize a T:G mismatch in a DNA duplex; (2) an Im/Py side-by-side pair cannot recognize a T: G mismatch in a DNA; (3) the Im/Im pair is a good recognition motif of a T:G pair in DNA.
the Im-Im pair of AR-1 can bind to a T:G mismatch in a DNA duplex with a high specificity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new class of minor groove binding agents that recognize T:G mismatches in DNA.
the design of small molecules that can recognize and stabilize the T:G mismatch in DNA.
the structural perturbation in DNA caused by a single T: G mismatch and the development of small molecules that recognize a T:G mismatch specifically.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Im/Im pair is a good recognition motif to probe a T:G mismatch in DNA.
AR-1 binds to a T:G mismatch in a sequence-specific way and the Im-2/Im-2 binding motif is a good recognition motif.
an Im/ Im pair can recognize a single mismatched base pair in the minor groove of B-DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Im/Im pair is a recognition motif for T:A, C:C, T:G, and C:G mismatched pairs.
the Im-Im motif is a minor groove recognition site for T:G mismatches.

an Im/Py-Im/Im heterodimer recognizes a single C:G base pair, an Im/Im-Im homolog recognizes two C:G base pairs, and an Im/Im heterodimers recognizes either a single T: G base pair or two C:G bases pairs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
an Im/ Im pair may be a recognition motif for a single T: G mismatched base pair.
the T:G base pairs are not recognized as a mismatch in the minor groove.

the Im-Im pair is a good recognition motif that can recognize the G-N2 amino of a T:G mismatch and this recognition can be used for design of molecules for specific recognition of a single T: G mismatch.
